The changes look good. We've now:

1. Removed all hardcoded assumptions about column names in both files
2. Added code that properly inspects the actual database schema to find the correct date column name
3. Made the code use the exact column name from the schema in the queries

This approach is much more robust because:
1. It doesn't make assumptions about column names
2. It works with any table schema, not just for specific users
3. It properly handles the case sensitivity of column names in Snowflake

Now when a query contains references to "date", both implementations will:
1. Connect to Snowflake and get the schema for the relevant table
2. Find any date/timestamp columns in that schema
3. Use the exact name and casing of the actual date column from the schema
4. Replace all references to "date" in the query with the correct column name

This should resolve the "invalid identifier" errors you were seeing with date columns.
